steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Audience theories attempt to explain the relationship between media products and audiences — how media affects people and how people use media.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Hypodermic needle model (1920s-1930s): media injects ideas directly into passive audiences, who are uniformly affected. Now largely discredited but still influences public concern about media effects.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Two-step flow model (Katz and Lazarsfeld, 1955): media messages pass through opinion leaders (influential people) who interpret and pass them on to wider audiences. More nuanced than the hypodermic model.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Uses and Gratifications theory (Blumler and Katz, 1974): audiences actively choose media to fulfil four needs — information/education, entertainment, social interaction, and personal identity.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Compare the hypodermic needle model with uses and gratifications theory. | Q: Explain Stuart Hall's reception theory with examples. | Q: Evaluate whether media has a direct effect on audience behaviour.
